text: The 3 AM alert proves a sign-in happened on the jump host's service account from an unapproved IP. It doesn't yet prove how that IP reached a port that shouldn't be internet-reachable at all.
Mara queries CommonSecurityLog for that source IP on port 3389. DeviceAction comes back Allow. The firewall didn't get bypassed -- it deliberately let this connection through.
The firewall's rule-hit history shows which rule matched: ALLOW-VENDOR-RDP-SUPPORT, the same rule built in Lesson 4 for the metering vendor's remote support.

That's the pivot. The firewall doesn't check whether this is really the vendor -- only whether the source IP falls inside the rule's configured range. A match means that range is wider than it should be.
The vendor connection itself is legitimate. What's wrong is narrower: a rule matching traffic it was never meant to match. Lesson 10 finds out exactly how wide.
